title.narrative: Cash Plus support for small holder farmers in Beletweyne-Enhancing lifesaving food security through cash and sustainable farming.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThrough this project, Action Against Hunger (ACF) will provide immediate and intermediate access to food for crisis and food insecure households in Beletweyne as per the SHF allocation 2025. The project will reach 2,573 HHs (1,261 male and 1,312 female) potentially reaching a total of 15,438 taking the average HH size of 6 in Somalia. The project is fully aligned to the SHF Standard Allocation 2025 and the Food Security Cluster guidelines. Adopting the Cash plus approach, a combination of unconditional cash transfers (UCT) and support to livelihood restoration activities through fast maturing food production and animal health services will be promoted. Households will be identified using the vulnerability-based targeting (VBT) approach. From ACF’s experience, VBT enhances inclusion as seen from the 2024 pilot that increased minority clan inclusion from 25% to 35% and PWD from 7% to 10% compared to the previous year. The project will target under-served riverine villages largely inhabited by the Somali Bantu ethnic minority that present the highest GAM levels in Beletweyne of 16.4% and have been at the center of cyclic flooding. Returning IDPs to targeted villages will also be prioritised. UCT will be used as an entry point to the food security. Favoring a participatory approach, ACF will be intentional in meaningful engagement of the targeted HHs including through inclusive and varied feedback mechanisms. The inputs will be determined in consultation with the farmers enough to farm a minimum of an acre. A mix of cereals and vegetable seeds will be distributed adapted to the riverine locations, increasing access to a nutritious and balanced diet. Gender and protection mainstreaming is intentional. All the proposed villages for the project are inhabited by the ethnic minority in Beletwyene. Apart from a full outcome around protection mainstreaming, ACF plans to ensure that at least 10% of the UCT target will be GBV survivors as referred from sister agencies through the GBV working group. ACF will consciously participate in intra and inter referrals, especially for the protection, health and nutrition components. ACF will monitor access barriers, service quality, and protection risks through client satisfaction surveys, call center data, and community consultations. PSEA will be promoted through appropriate information sessions to targeted HHs on identification of and obligation to report of SEA cases. ltbrgtlt/pgt
